description:
The two measurement records that a committed self-test script depends on are pinned to their current commit, so container archival retains them at their present paths instead of relocating them.

## Background

`scripts/benchmark-session-cost-selftest.sh` opens `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` by path at runtime. That record and its sibling `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-c488ef85.json` are linked to terminal issues inside a container whose archival run would otherwise move them out from under the script.

The mechanism already has the right instrument: a document reference pinned to a commit is treated as a historical reference and retained rather than relocated. Pinning keeps the traceability from the owning issues to the records they produced, which unlinking would destroy.

The pin is:

- `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-27ffbd2d.json` on issue `73981310` — pinned to the commit that holds its current content.
- `dev/studies/perf/session-cost-c488ef85.json` on issue `a4b0fadf` — pinned to the commit that holds its current content.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Both named document references are pinned to a commit and still name their owning issues.
- [hard] REQ-02: An archival preview for the container that owns them reports both records as retained rather than relocated.
- [hard] REQ-03: The self-test script resolves the measurement record it opens at runtime.
- [hard] REQ-04: Whole-repository validation passes afterwards.
title: Pin the runtime-read measurement records so archival retains them
